finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice by ID with no ownership check, so it is an IDOR. The sibling /my/invoice route enforces the owner check, which shows it was intended.
finding.source: inv_id URL path parameter, controlled by any requester
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record

trace.note: INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the invoice globally, with no customer filter
the invoice is returned without comparing inv['customer'] to g.user['id']

finding.guards_checked: There is no authentication decorator, no before_request hook in the file, no ownership comparison and no role check. The check in get_my_invoice (line 16) is absent here. Whether g.user is populated elsewhere cannot be seen, and this route does not use it. If invoice IDs are guessable or sequential, enumeration is trivial.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:9-10 fetches INVOICES.get(inv_id) and returns it via jsonify with no auth decorator, before_request hook, or inv["customer"] vs g.user["id"] check, unlike the sibling check at invoices.py:16. Any requester, even an anonymous one, can read any invoice, and invoices.py is the only file in the directory.
